reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7199, 7200, book 93, باب كَيْفَ يُبَايِعُ الإِمَامُ النَّاسَ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ، حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي عُبَادَةُ بْنُ الْوَلِيدِ، أَخْبَرَنِي أَبِي، عَنْ عُبَادَةَ بْنِ الصَّامِتِ، قَالَ "بَايَعْنَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى السَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ فِي الْمَنْشَطِ وَالْمَكْرَهِ‏.‏ ‏‏وَأَنْ لاَ نُنَازِعَ الأَمْرَ أَهْلَهُ، وَأَنْ نَقُومَ ـ أَوْ نَقُولَ ـ بِالْحَقِّ حَيْثُمَا كُنَّا لاَ نَخَافُ فِي اللَّهِ لَوْمَةَ لاَئِمٍ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Ismail narrated to me; Malik narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Said, who said: Ubadah ibn al-Walid informed me; my father informed me, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: We pledged to the Messenger of Allah to listen and obey in ease and hardship, not to dispute authority with those entitled to it, and to stand—or speak—for the truth wherever we were, not fearing the blame of anyone for Allah’s sake.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7201, book 93, باب كَيْفَ يُبَايِعُ الإِمَامُ النَّاسَ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ عَلِيٍّ، حَدَّثَنَا خَالِدُ بْنُ الْحَارِثِ، حَدَّثَنَا حُمَيْدٌ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ خَرَجَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي غَدَاةٍ بَارِدَةٍ وَالْمُهَاجِرُونَ وَالأَنْصَارُ يَحْفِرُونَ الْخَنْدَقَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّ الْخَيْرَ خَيْرُ الآخِرَهْ فَاغْفِرْ لِلأَنْصَارِ وَالْمُهَاجِرَهْ ‏"‏ فَأَجَابُوا نَحْنُ الَّذِينَ بَايَعُوا مُحَمَّدَا عَلَى الْجِهَادِ مَا بَقِينَا أَبَدَا
en_text: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us; Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us; Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: The Prophet came out on a cold morning while the Emigrants and the Ansar were digging the trench. He said: “O Allah, the true good is the good of the Hereafter, so forgive the Ansar and the Emigrants.” They replied: “We are those who pledged to Muhammad to strive in jihad for as long as we live.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7202, book 93, باب كَيْفَ يُبَايِعُ الإِمَامُ النَّاسَ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَالِكٌ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ دِينَارٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كُنَّا إِذَا بَايَعْنَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى السَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ يَقُولُ لَنَا ‏"‏ فِيمَا اسْتَطَعْتَ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Malik informed us, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: When we pledged to the Messenger of Allah to listen and obey, he would say to us: “As far as you are able.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7203, book 93, باب كَيْفَ يُبَايِعُ الإِمَامُ النَّاسَ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى، عَنْ سُفْيَانَ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ دِينَارٍ، قَالَ شَهِدْتُ ابْنَ عُمَرَ حَيْثُ اجْتَمَعَ النَّاسُ عَلَى عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ ـ قَالَ ـ كَتَبَ إِنِّي أُقِرُّ بِالسَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ لِعَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَى سُنَّةِ اللَّهِ وَسُنَّةِ رَسُولِهِ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، وَإِنَّ بَنِيَّ قَدْ أَقَرُّوا بِمِثْلِ ذَلِكَ‏.‏
en_text: Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan; Abdullah ibn Dinar narrated to us, who said: I was present when the people gathered around Abd al-Malik. Ibn Umar wrote: “I acknowledge listening and obedience to Abd al-Malik, Commander of the Faithful, according to the Sunnah of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, as far as I am able. My sons have acknowledged the same.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7204, book 93, باب كَيْفَ يُبَايِعُ الإِمَامُ النَّاسَ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا يَعْقُوبُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، حَدَّثَنَا هُشَيْمٌ، أَخْبَرَنَا سَيَّارٌ، عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، عَنْ جَرِيرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ بَايَعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى السَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ، فَلَقَّنَنِي، فِيمَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، وَالنُّصْحِ لِكُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ‏.‏
en_text: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Hushaym narrated to us; Sayyar informed us, from al-Shabi, from Jarir ibn Abdullah, who said: I pledged to the Prophet to listen and obey. He instructed me to add, “as far as you are able,” and to give sincere counsel to every Muslim.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7205, book 93, باب كَيْفَ يُبَايِعُ الإِمَامُ النَّاسَ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ عَلِيٍّ، حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى، عَنْ سُفْيَانَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ دِينَارٍ، قَالَ لَمَّا بَايَعَ النَّاسُ عَبْدَ الْمَلِكِ كَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ إِلَى عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنِّي أُقِرُّ بِالسَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ لِعَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، عَلَى سُنَّةِ اللَّهِ وَسُنَّةِ رَسُولِهِ، فِيمَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، وَإِنَّ بَنِيَّ قَدْ أَقَرُّوا بِذَلِكَ‏.‏
en_text: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: Abdullah ibn Dinar narrated to me. He said: When the people pledged allegiance to Abd al-Malik, Abdullah ibn Umar wrote to him: “To Abdullah Abd al-Malik, Commander of the Faithful: I acknowledge listening and obedience to you, according to the Sunnah of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, as far as I am able. My sons have acknowledged this as well.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7206, book 93, باب كَيْفَ يُبَايِعُ الإِمَامُ النَّاسَ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا حَاتِمٌ، عَنْ يَزِيدَ، قَالَ قُلْتُ لِسَلَمَةَ عَلَى أَىِّ شَىْءٍ بَايَعْتُمُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَوْمَ الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ قَالَ عَلَى الْمَوْتِ‏.‏
en_text: Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us; Hatim narrated to us, from Yazid, who said: I asked Salamah, “What did you pledge to the Prophet on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah?” He said, “We pledged to die.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7207, book 93, باب كَيْفَ يُبَايِعُ الإِمَامُ النَّاسَ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَسْمَاءَ، حَدَّثَنَا جُوَيْرِيَةُ، عَنْ مَالِكٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، أَنَّ حُمَيْدَ بْنَ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّ الْمِسْوَرَ بْنَ مَخْرَمَةَ أَخْبَرَهُ‏.‏ أَنَّ الرَّهْطَ الَّذِينَ وَلاَّهُمْ عُمَرُ اجْتَمَعُوا فَتَشَاوَرُوا، قَالَ لَهُمْ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ لَسْتُ بِالَّذِي أُنَافِسُكُمْ عَلَى هَذَا الأَمْرِ، وَلَكِنَّكُمْ إِنْ شِئْتُمُ اخْتَرْتُ لَكُمْ مِنْكُمْ‏.‏ فَجَعَلُوا ذَلِكَ إِلَى عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، فَلَمَّا وَلَّوْا عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ أَمْرَهُمْ فَمَالَ النَّاسُ عَلَى عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، حَتَّى مَا أَرَى أَحَدًا مِنَ النَّاسِ يَتْبَعُ أُولَئِكَ الرَّهْطَ وَلاَ يَطَأُ عَقِبَهُ، وَمَالَ النَّاسُ عَلَى عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ يُشَاوِرُونَهُ تِلْكَ اللَّيَالِيَ حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الَّتِي أَصْبَحْنَا مِنْهَا، فَبَايَعْنَا عُثْمَانَ قَالَ الْمِسْوَرُ طَرَقَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بَعْدَ هَجْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَضَرَبَ الْبَابَ حَتَّى اسْتَيْقَظْتُ فَقَالَ أَرَاكَ نَائِمًا، فَوَاللَّهِ مَا اكْتَحَلْتُ هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ بِكَبِيرِ نَوْمٍ، انْطَلِقْ فَادْعُ الزُّبَيْرَ وَسَعْدًا، فَدَعَوْتُهُمَا لَهُ فَشَاوَرَهُمَا ثُمَّ دَعَانِي فَقَالَ ادْعُ لِي عَلِيًّا‏.‏ فَدَعَوْتُهُ فَنَاجَاهُ حَتَّى ابْهَارَّ اللَّيْلُ، ثُمَّ قَامَ عَلِيٌّ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ، وَهْوَ عَلَى طَمَعٍ، وَقَدْ كَانَ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ يَخْشَى مِنْ عَلِيٍّ شَيْئًا، ثُمَّ قَالَ ادْعُ لِي عُثْمَانَ، فَدَعَوْتُهُ فَنَاجَاهُ حَتَّى فَرَّقَ بَيْنَهُمَا الْمُؤَذِّنُ بِالصُّبْحِ، فَلَمَّا صَلَّى لِلنَّاسِ الصُّبْحَ وَاجْتَمَعَ أُولَئِكَ الرَّهْطُ عِنْدَ الْمِنْبَرِ، فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى مَنْ كَانَ حَاضِرًا مِنَ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالأَنْصَارِ، وَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى أُمَرَاءِ الأَجْنَادِ وَكَانُوا وَافَوْا تِلْكَ الْحَجَّةَ مَعَ عُمَرَ، فَلَمَّا اجْتَمَعُوا تَشَهَّدَ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَمَّا بَعْدُ يَا عَلِيُّ، إِنِّي قَدْ نَظَرْتُ فِي أَمْرِ النَّاسِ فَلَمْ أَرَهُمْ يَعْدِلُونَ بِعُثْمَانَ، فَلاَ تَجْعَلَنَّ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ سَبِيلاً‏.‏ فَقَالَ أُبَايِعُكَ عَلَى سُنَّةِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالْخَلِيفَتَيْنِ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ‏.‏ فَبَايَعَهُ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ، وَبَايَعَهُ النَّاسُ الْمُهَاجِرُونَ وَالأَنْصَارُ وَأُمَرَاءُ الأَجْنَادِ وَالْمُسْلِمُونَ‏.‏
en_text: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma narrated to us; Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Malik, from al-Zuhri, that Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman informed him that al-Miswar ibn Makhramah informed him: The group whom Umar had appointed gathered and consulted one another. Abd al-Rahman said to them, “I am not competing with you for this matter, but if you wish, I will choose one of you for you.” They entrusted the decision to Abd al-Rahman. When they put him in charge of their affair, people gathered around him, so much so that I saw no one following those men or walking behind them; instead, people flocked to Abd al-Rahman and consulted him during those nights. When the night came before the morning on which we pledged allegiance to Uthman, Abd al-Rahman came to me after part of the night had passed and knocked until I awoke. He said, “I see you are sleeping. By Allah, I have hardly slept at all tonight. Go and call al-Zubayr and Sad.” I called them, and he consulted them. Then he called me and said, “Call Ali.” I called him, and Abd al-Rahman spoke privately with him until the night was very late. Ali then left, still hopeful, though Abd al-Rahman had some concern about Ali. Then Abd al-Rahman said, “Call Uthman.” I called him, and he spoke privately with him until the dawn caller separated them. After Abd al-Rahman led the people in the dawn prayer, the appointed group gathered by the pulpit. He sent for the Emigrants and Ansar who were present and for the commanders of the armies who had come on that pilgrimage with Umar. When they had assembled, Abd al-Rahman testified and said: “Now then, Ali, I have considered the people’s affairs and have not seen them prefer anyone over Uthman. Do not create a way against yourself.” Ali said: “I pledge allegiance to you on the basis of the Sunnah of Allah and His Messenger and the two caliphs after him.” Abd al-Rahman pledged allegiance to him, and the Emigrants, Ansar, army commanders, and Muslims pledged allegiance.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7208, book 93, باب مَنْ بَايَعَ مَرَّتَيْنِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَاصِمٍ، عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ أَبِي عُبَيْدٍ، عَنْ سَلَمَةَ، قَالَ بَايَعْنَا النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ فَقَالَ لِي ‏"‏ يَا سَلَمَةُ أَلاَ تُبَايِعُ ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَدْ بَايَعْتُ فِي الأَوَّلِ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ وَفِي الثَّانِي ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd, from Salamah, who said: We pledged allegiance to the Prophet beneath the tree. He said to me, “Salamah, will you not pledge allegiance?” I said, “Messenger of Allah, I pledged allegiance the first time.” He said, “And do so the second time.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7209, book 93, باب بَيْعَةِ الأَعْرَابِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ، عَنْ مَالِكٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ أَنَّ أَعْرَابِيًّا بَايَعَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى الإِسْلاَمِ، فَأَصَابَهُ وَعْكٌ فَقَالَ أَقِلْنِي بَيْعَتِي‏.‏ فَأَبَى، ثُمَّ جَاءَهُ فَقَالَ أَقِلْنِي بَيْعَتِي‏.‏ فَأَبَى، فَخَرَجَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ الْمَدِينَةُ كَالْكِيرِ، تَنْفِي خَبَثَهَا، وَيَنْصَعُ طِيبُهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us, from Malik, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both: A Bedouin pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah upon Islam, then he was struck by fever. He said, “Release me from my pledge.” The Prophet refused. The man came again and said, “Release me from my pledge,” but he refused. The man then left. The Messenger of Allah said: “Madinah is like a furnace: it removes its impurities and its good becomes pure.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7210, book 93, باب بَيْعَةِ الصَّغِيرِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدٌ ـ هُوَ ابْنُ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ ـ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو عَقِيلٍ، زُهْرَةُ بْنُ مَعْبَدٍ عَنْ جَدِّهِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ هِشَامٍ، وَكَانَ، قَدْ أَدْرَكَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَذَهَبَتْ بِهِ أُمُّهُ زَيْنَبُ ابْنَةُ حُمَيْدٍ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ بَايِعْهُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ هُوَ صَغِيرٌ ‏"‏ فَمَسَحَ رَأْسَهُ وَدَعَا لَهُ، وَكَانَ يُضَحِّي بِالشَّاةِ الْوَاحِدَةِ عَنْ جَمِيعِ أَهْلِهِ‏.‏
en_text: Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us; Said (meaning Ibn Abi Ayyub) narrated to us, who said: Abu Aqil, Zuhrah ibn Mabid, narrated to me, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn Hisham, who had met the Prophet. His mother, Zaynab daughter of Humayd, took him to the Messenger of Allah and said, “Messenger of Allah, accept his pledge.” The Prophet said: “He is still a child.” He wiped his head and prayed for him. He used to offer one sheep as a sacrifice on behalf of all his family.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7211, book 93, باب مَنْ بَايَعَ ثُمَّ اسْتَقَالَ الْبَيْعَةَ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَالِكٌ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ،‏.‏ أَنَّ أَعْرَابِيًّا، بَايَعَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى الإِسْلاَمِ فَأَصَابَ الأَعْرَابِيَّ وَعْكٌ بِالْمَدِينَةِ، فَأَتَى الأَعْرَابِيُّ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَقِلْنِي بَيْعَتِي، فَأَبَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ جَاءَهُ فَقَالَ أَقِلْنِي بَيْعَتِي فَأَبَى، ثُمَّ جَاءَهُ فَقَالَ أَقِلْنِي بَيْعَتِي فَأَبَى فَخَرَجَ الأَعْرَابِيُّ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّمَا الْمَدِينَةُ كَالْكِيرِ تَنْفِي خَبَثَهَا وَيَنْصَعُ طِيبُهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Malik informed us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah: A Bedouin pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah upon Islam, then fever struck him in Madinah. He came to the Messenger of Allah and said, “Messenger of Allah, release me from my pledge.” The Messenger of Allah refused. He came again and said, “Release me from my pledge,” and he refused. He came a third time and said, “Release me from my pledge,” and he refused. The Bedouin then left. The Messenger of Allah said: “Madinah is like a furnace: it removes its impurities and its good becomes pure.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7212, book 93, باب مَنْ بَايَعَ رَجُلاً لاَ يُبَايِعُهُ إِلاَّ لِلدُّنْيَا
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدَانُ، عَنْ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ أَبِي صَالِحٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ ثَلاَثَةٌ لاَ يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَلاَ يُزَكِّيهِمْ، وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ رَجُلٌ عَلَى فَضْلِ مَاءٍ بِالطَّرِيقِ يَمْنَعُ مِنْهُ ابْنَ السَّبِيلِ، وَرَجُلٌ بَايَعَ إِمَامًا لاَ يُبَايِعُهُ إِلاَّ لِدُنْيَاهُ، إِنْ أَعْطَاهُ مَا يُرِيدُ وَفَى لَهُ، وَإِلاَّ لَمْ يَفِ لَهُ، وَرَجُلٌ يُبَايِعُ رَجُلاً بِسِلْعَةٍ بَعْدَ الْعَصْرِ فَحَلَفَ بِاللَّهِ لَقَدْ أُعْطِيَ بِهَا كَذَا وَكَذَا فَصَدَّقَهُ، فَأَخَذَهَا، وَلَمْ يُعْطَ بِهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Abdan narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from al-Amash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “There are three to whom Allah will not speak on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and for whom there will be a painful punishment: a man who has surplus water on a road and withholds it from a traveler; a man who pledges allegiance to a leader only for worldly gain, so that if he gives him what he wants he keeps faith with him, but if not, he does not; and a man who makes a sale to another after the afternoon prayer, swears by Allah that he was offered such-and-such for it, and the buyer believes him and takes it, although he was not offered that amount.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7213, book 93, باب بَيْعَةِ النِّسَاءِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْيَمَانِ، أَخْبَرَنَا شُعَيْبٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، وَقَالَ اللَّيْثُ، حَدَّثَنِي يُونُسُ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، أَخْبَرَنِي أَبُو إِدْرِيسَ الْخَوْلاَنِيُّ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ عُبَادَةَ بْنَ الصَّامِتِ، يَقُولُ قَالَ لَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَنَحْنُ فِي مَجْلِسٍ ‏"‏ تُبَايِعُونِي عَلَى أَنْ لاَ تُشْرِكُوا بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا، وَلاَ تَسْرِقُوا، وَلاَ تَزْنُوا، وَلاَ تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلاَدَكُمْ، وَلاَ تَأْتُوا بِبُهْتَانٍ تَفْتَرُونَهُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَأَرْجُلِكُمْ وَلاَ تَعْصُوا فِي مَعْرُوفٍ، فَمَنْ وَفَى مِنْكُمْ فَأَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، وَمَنْ أَصَابَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْئًا فَعُوقِبَ فِي الدُّنْيَا فَهْوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لَهُ، وَمَنْ أَصَابَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْئًا فَسَتَرَهُ اللَّهُ فَأَمْرُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ إِنْ شَاءَ عَاقَبَهُ وَإِنْ شَاءَ عَفَا عَنْهُ ‏"‏، فَبَايَعْنَاهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ‏.‏
en_text: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Shuaib informed us, from al-Zuhri. Al-Layth said: Yunus narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who informed me that Abu Idris al-Khawlani heard Ubadah ibn al-Samit say: The Messenger of Allah said to us while we were gathered: “Will you pledge to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, steal, commit adultery, kill your children, bring a false accusation that you fabricate between your hands and legs, or disobey in what is right? Whoever among you fulfills this, his reward is with Allah. Whoever commits any of these acts and is punished for it in this world, that punishment is an expiation for him. Whoever commits any of them and Allah conceals it, then his case rests with Allah: if He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him.” So we pledged to him on that basis.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7214, book 93, باب بَيْعَةِ النِّسَاءِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مَحْمُودٌ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ ـ رضى الله عنها ـ قَالَتْ كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُبَايِعُ النِّسَاءَ بِالْكَلاَمِ بِهَذِهِ الآيَةِ ‏[quran sura="60" aya_start="12" aya_end="12"]{‏لاَ يُشْرِكْنَ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا‏}‏ قَالَتْ وَمَا مَسَّتْ يَدُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَدَ امْرَأَةٍ، إِلاَّ امْرَأَةً يَمْلِكُهَا‏.‏
en_text: Mahmud narrated to us; Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet used to accept women’s pledges verbally, in accordance with this verse: “that they will not associate anything with Allah” (60:12). Aishah said: The Messenger of Allah’s hand never touched a woman’s hand, except a woman whom he owned.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7215, book 93, باب بَيْعَةِ النِّسَاءِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ حَفْصَةَ، عَنْ أُمِّ عَطِيَّةَ، قَالَتْ بَايَعْنَا النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَرَأَ عَلَىَّ ‏[quran sura="60" aya_start="12" aya_end="12"]{‏أَنْ لاَ يُشْرِكْنَ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا‏}‏ وَنَهَانَا عَنِ النِّيَاحَةِ، فَقَبَضَتِ امْرَأَةٌ مِنَّا يَدَهَا فَقَالَتْ فُلاَنَةُ أَسْعَدَتْنِي وَأَنَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَجْزِيَهَا، فَلَمْ يَقُلْ شَيْئًا، ثُمَّ رَجَعَتْ، فَمَا وَفَتِ امْرَأَةٌ إِلاَّ أُمُّ سُلَيْمٍ وَأُمُّ الْعَلاَءِ، وَابْنَةُ أَبِي سَبْرَةَ امْرَأَةُ مُعَاذٍ أَوِ ابْنَةُ أَبِي سَبْرَةَ وَامْرَأَةُ مُعَاذٍ‏.‏
en_text: Musaddad narrated to us; Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Hafsah, from Umm Atiyyah, who said: We pledged allegiance to the Prophet, and he recited to me: “that they will not associate anything with Allah” (60:12). He forbade us to lament the dead. One woman among us withdrew her hand and said, “So-and-so comforted me, and I want to repay her.” He said nothing. She later returned. None of the women fulfilled the pledge except Umm Sulaym, Umm al-Ala, and the daughter of Abu Sabrah, the wife of Muadh—or the daughter of Abu Sabrah and the wife of Muadh.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7216, book 93, باب مَنْ نَكَثَ بَيْعَةً
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو نُعَيْمٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، سَمِعْتُ جَابِرًا، قَالَ جَاءَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ بَايِعْنِي عَلَى الإِسْلاَمِ‏.‏ فَبَايَعَهُ عَلَى الإِسْلاَمِ، ثُمَّ جَاءَ الْغَدَ مَحْمُومًا فَقَالَ أَقِلْنِي‏.‏ فَأَبَى، فَلَمَّا وَلَّى قَالَ ‏"‏ الْمَدِينَةُ كَالْكِيرِ، تَنْفِي خَبَثَهَا، وَيَنْصَعُ طِيبُهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Abu Nuaym narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir say: A Bedouin came to the Prophet and said, “Accept my pledge to Islam.” He accepted his pledge. The next day the man came with a fever and said, “Release me from it.” The Prophet refused. When the man turned away, he said: “Madinah is like a furnace: it removes its impurities and its good becomes pure.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7217, book 93, باب الاِسْتِخْلاَفِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ يَحْيَى، أَخْبَرَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ بِلاَلٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، سَمِعْتُ الْقَاسِمَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ ـ رضى الله عنها ـ وَارَأْسَاهْ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ ذَاكِ لَوْ كَانَ وَأَنَا حَىٌّ فَأَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكِ وَأَدْعُو لَكِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ وَاثُكْلِيَاهْ وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لأَظُنُّكَ تُحِبُّ مَوْتِي وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَاكَ لَظَلِلْتَ آخِرَ يَوْمِكَ مُعَرِّسًا بِبَعْضِ أَزْوَاجِكَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ بَلْ أَنَا وَارَأْسَاهْ لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ ـ أَوْ أَرَدْتُ ـ أَنْ أُرْسِلَ إِلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ وَابْنِهِ فَأَعْهَدَ أَنْ يَقُولَ الْقَائِلُونَ أَوْ يَتَمَنَّى الْمُتَمَنُّونَ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ قُلْتُ يَأْبَى اللَّهُ وَيَدْفَعُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ، أَوْ يَدْفَعُ اللَّهُ وَيَأْبَى الْمُؤْمِنُونَ‏.‏
en_text: Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us; Sulayman ibn Bilal informed us, from Yahya ibn Said, who said: I heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say that Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said, “Oh, my head!” The Messenger of Allah said: “That would be no problem if it happened while I was alive; I would ask Allah to forgive you and pray for you.” Aishah said, “What a loss! By Allah, I think you want me to die. If that happened, you would spend the rest of that day with one of your wives.” The Prophet said: “No, it is I who say, ‘Oh, my head!’ I had intended—or wanted—to send for Abu Bakr and his son and make a stipulation, lest someone make claims or wish for things.” Then I said, “Allah will not allow it, and the believers will prevent it,” or, “Allah will prevent it, and the believers will not allow it.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7218, book 93, باب الاِسْتِخْلاَفِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، أَخْبَرَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ قِيلَ لِعُمَرَ أَلاَ تَسْتَخْلِفُ قَالَ إِنْ أَسْتَخْلِفْ فَقَدِ اسْتَخْلَفَ مَنْ هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِنِّي أَبُو بَكْرٍ، وَإِنْ أَتْرُكْ فَقَدْ تَرَكَ مَنْ هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَثْنَوْا عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ رَاغِبٌ رَاهِبٌ، وَدِدْتُ أَنِّي نَجَوْتُ مِنْهَا كَفَافًا لاَ لِي وَلاَ عَلَىَّ لاَ أَتَحَمَّلُهَا حَيًّا وَمَيِّتًا‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Sufyan informed us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: Umar was asked, “Will you appoint a successor?” He said: “If I appoint one, someone better than me, Abu Bakr, appointed a successor. If I leave it, someone better than me, the Messenger of Allah, left it.” They praised him, and he said: “I am neither eager for it nor seeking to escape it. I wish I could be free of it with neither gain nor blame, and not have to bear it alive or dead.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7219, book 93, باب الاِسْتِخْلاَفِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مُوسَى، أَخْبَرَنَا هِشَامٌ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، أَخْبَرَنِي أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ خُطْبَةَ، عُمَرَ الآخِرَةَ حِينَ جَلَسَ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ، وَذَلِكَ الْغَدُ مِنْ يَوْمٍ تُوُفِّيَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَتَشَهَّدَ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ صَامِتٌ لاَ يَتَكَلَّمُ قَالَ كُنْتُ أَرْجُو أَنْ يَعِيشَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى يَدْبُرَنَا ـ يُرِيدُ بِذَلِكَ أَنْ يَكُونَ آخِرَهُمْ ـ فَإِنْ يَكُ مُحَمَّدٌ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَدْ مَاتَ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى قَدْ جَعَلَ بَيْنَ أَظْهُرِكُمْ نُورًا تَهْتَدُونَ بِهِ بِمَا هَدَى اللَّهُ مُحَمَّدًا صلى الله عليه وسلم وَإِنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ صَاحِبُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثَانِي اثْنَيْنِ، فَإِنَّهُ أَوْلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ بِأُمُورِكُمْ، فَقُومُوا فَبَايِعُوهُ‏.‏ وَكَانَتْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ قَدْ بَايَعُوهُ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ فِي سَقِيفَةِ بَنِي سَاعِدَةَ، وَكَانَتْ بَيْعَةُ الْعَامَّةِ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ‏.‏ قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ سَمِعْتُ عُمَرَ يَقُولُ لأَبِي بَكْرٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ اصْعَدِ الْمِنْبَرَ‏.‏ فَلَمْ يَزَلْ بِهِ حَتَّى صَعِدَ الْمِنْبَرَ، فَبَايَعَهُ النَّاسُ عَامَّةً‏.‏
en_text: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us; Hisham informed us, from Mamar, from al-Zuhri. Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, informed me that he heard Umar’s final sermon when Umar sat on the pulpit, the day after the Prophet died. Umar testified, while Abu Bakr remained silent and did not speak: “I had hoped that the Messenger of Allah would live until he was the last of us to die. If Muhammad has died, Allah has left among you a light by which you are guided, through what Allah guided Muhammad. Abu Bakr is the Companion of the Messenger of Allah, the second of the two, and the most entitled among the Muslims to manage your affairs. So stand and pledge allegiance to him.” Some people had already pledged to him at the portico of Banu Saidah; the public pledge was on the pulpit. Al-Zuhri reported from Anas ibn Malik that Umar said to Abu Bakr that day, “Ascend the pulpit.” Umar kept urging him until he ascended it, and the people at large pledged allegiance to him.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7220, book 93, باب الاِسْتِخْلاَفِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرِ بْنِ مُطْعِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ أَتَتِ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم امْرَأَةٌ فَكَلَّمَتْهُ فِي شَىْءٍ فَأَمَرَهَا أَنْ تَرْجِعَ إِلَيْهِ، قَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ جِئْتُ وَلَمْ أَجِدْكَ، كَأَنَّهَا تُرِيدُ الْمَوْتَ، قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنْ لَمْ تَجِدِينِي فَأْتِي أَبَا بَكْرٍ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mutim, from his father, who said: A woman came to the Prophet and spoke to him about something. He told her to return to him. She said, “Messenger of Allah, what if I come and do not find you?”—as if she meant his death. He said: “If you do not find me, then go to Abu Bakr.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7221, book 93, باب الاِسْتِخْلاَفِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى، عَنْ سُفْيَانَ، حَدَّثَنِي قَيْسُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ، عَنْ طَارِقِ بْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ لِوَفْدِ بُزَاخَةَ تَتْبَعُونَ أَذْنَابَ الإِبِلِ حَتَّى يُرِيَ اللَّهُ خَلِيفَةَ نَبِيِّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَالْمُهَاجِرِينَ أَمْرًا يَعْذِرُونَكُمْ بِهِ‏.‏
en_text: Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan; Qays ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said to the delegation of Buzakhah: “You will follow the camels’ trails until Allah shows the successor of His Prophet and the Emigrants a course of action toward you for which they may excuse you.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7222, 7223, book 93, كتاب الأحكام
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، حَدَّثَنَا غُنْدَرٌ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ، سَمِعْتُ جَابِرَ بْنَ سَمُرَةَ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏"‏ يَكُونُ اثْنَا عَشَرَ أَمِيرًا ـ فَقَالَ كَلِمَةً لَمْ أَسْمَعْهَا فَقَالَ أَبِي إِنَّهُ قَالَ ـ كُلُّهُمْ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me; Ghundar narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Samurah say: I heard the Prophet say: “There will be twelve commanders.” He said a word I did not hear. My father said he said: “All of them will be from Quraysh.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7224, book 93, باب إِخْرَاجِ الْخُصُومِ وَأَهْلِ الرِّيَبِ مِنَ الْبُيُوتِ بَعْدَ الْمَعْرِفَةِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ، حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنْ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ، عَنِ الأَعْرَجِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ أَنْ آمُرَ بِحَطَبٍ يُحْتَطَبُ، ثُمَّ آمُرَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فَيُؤَذَّنَ لَهَا، ثُمَّ آمُرَ رَجُلاً فَيَؤُمَّ النَّاسَ، ثُمَّ أُخَالِفَ إِلَى رِجَالٍ فَأُحَرِّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ بُيُوتَهُمْ، وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ لَوْ يَعْلَمُ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنَّهُ يَجِدُ عَرْقًا سَمِينًا أَوْ مَرْمَاتَيْنِ حَسَنَتَيْنِ لَشَهِدَ الْعِشَاءَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ قَالَ يُونُسُ قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ مِرْمَاةٌ مَا بَيْنَ ظِلْفِ الشَّاةِ مِنَ اللَّحْمِ مِثْلُ مِنْسَاةٍ وَمِيضَاةٍ‏.‏ الْمِيمُ مَخْفُوضَةٌ‏.‏
en_text: Ismail narrated to us; Malik narrated to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I considered ordering firewood to be gathered, then ordering the prayer and having the call made for it, then appointing a man to lead the people in prayer, and then going to men who stay behind and burning their houses over them. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if one of them knew that he would find a meaty bone or two good pieces of meat, he would attend the evening prayer.” Muhammad ibn Yusuf said: Yunus said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman said: Abu Abdullah explained that a mirmah is a piece of meat between the sheep’s hoof, like a small stick; the meem is vowelled with kasrah.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7225, book 93, بَابُ هَلْ لِلإِمَامِ أَنْ يَمْنَعَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ وَأَهْلَ الْمَعْصِيَةِ مِنَ الْكَلاَمِ مَعَهُ وَالزِّيَارَةِ وَنَحْوِهِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا اللَّيْثُ، عَنْ عُقَيْلٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ كَعْبِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ كَعْبِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ ـ وَكَانَ قَائِدَ كَعْبٍ مِنْ بَنِيهِ حِينَ عَمِيَ ـ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ كَعْبَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ لَمَّا تَخَلَّفَ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي غَزْوَةِ تَبُوكَ ـ فَذَكَرَ حَدِيثَهُ ـ وَنَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْمُسْلِمِينَ عَنْ كَلاَمِنَا، فَلَبِثْنَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ خَمْسِينَ لَيْلَةً، وَآذَنَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِتَوْبَةِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْنَا‏.‏
en_text: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to me; al-Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Kab ibn Malik, that Abdullah ibn Kab ibn Malik—who used to guide his father Kab, who had become blind—said: I heard Kab ibn Malik say: When he stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah during the expedition to Tabuk, he related his account. The Messenger of Allah forbade the Muslims to speak to us, and we remained in that state for fifty nights. Then the Messenger of Allah announced that Allah had accepted our repentance.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7226, book 94, باب مَا جَاءَ فِي التَّمَنِّي وَمَنْ تَمَنَّى الشَّهَادَةَ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ عُفَيْرٍ، حَدَّثَنِي اللَّيْثُ، حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ خَالِدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، وَسَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ، أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏"‏ وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ لَوْلاَ أَنَّ رِجَالاً يَكْرَهُونَ أَنْ يَتَخَلَّفُوا بَعْدِي وَلاَ أَجِدُ مَا أَحْمِلُهُمْ مَا تَخَلَّفْتُ، لَوَدِدْتُ أَنِّي أُقْتَلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، ثُمَّ أُحْيَا ثُمَّ أُقْتَلُ، ثُمَّ أُحْيَا ثُمَّ أُقْتَلُ، ثُمَّ أُحْيَا ثُمَّ أُقْتَلُ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Said ibn Ufayr narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to me; Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah and Said ibn al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, were it not that some men dislike being left behind after me, and that I have no mounts to carry them, I would not remain behind from any expedition. I would love to be killed in the path of Allah, then brought back to life, then killed, then brought back to life, then killed.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7227, book 94, باب مَا جَاءَ فِي التَّمَنِّي وَمَنْ تَمَنَّى الشَّهَادَةَ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَالِكٌ، عَنْ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ، عَنِ الأَعْرَجِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ وَدِدْتُ أَنِّي لأُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَأُقْتَلُ ثُمَّ أُحْيَا ثُمَّ أُقْتَلُ، ثُمَّ أُحْيَا، ثُمَّ أُقْتَلُ، ثُمَّ أُحْيَا، ثُمَّ أُقْتَلُ، ثُمَّ أُحْيَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَكَانَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ يَقُولُهُنَّ ثَلاَثًا أَشْهَدُ بِاللَّهِ‏.‏
en_text: Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I would love to fight in the path of Allah and be killed, then be brought back to life, then be killed, then brought back to life, then be killed, then be brought back to life.” Abu Hurayrah used to say these words three times, affirming: “I swear by Allah.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7228, book 94, باب تَمَنِّي الْخَيْرِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ نَصْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ هَمَّامٍ، سَمِعَ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ لَوْ كَانَ عِنْدِي أُحُدٌ ذَهَبًا، لأَحْبَبْتُ أَنْ لاَ يَأْتِيَ ثَلاَثٌ وَعِنْدِي مِنْهُ دِينَارٌ، لَيْسَ شَىْءٌ أُرْصِدُهُ فِي دَيْنٍ عَلَىَّ أَجِدُ مَنْ يَقْبَلُهُ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Ishaq ibn Nasr narrated to us; Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Mamar, from Hammam, who heard Abu Hurayrah narrate from the Prophet, who said: “If I had gold equal to Mount Uhud, I would love for three nights not to pass while I still had any of it with me, except something I set aside to repay a debt, if I could find someone to accept it.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7229, book 94, باب قَوْلِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لَوِ اسْتَقْبَلْتُ مِنْ أَمْرِي مَا اسْتَدْبَرْتُ ‏"‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا اللَّيْثُ، عَنْ عُقَيْلٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، حَدَّثَنِي عُرْوَةُ، أَنَّ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لَوِ اسْتَقْبَلْتُ مِنْ أَمْرِي مَا اسْتَدْبَرْتُ مَا سُقْتُ الْهَدْىَ، وَلَحَلَلْتُ مَعَ النَّاسِ حِينَ حَلُّوا ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Urwah told me that Aishah said: The Messenger of Allah said: “If I had known beforehand what I later came to know, I would not have brought the sacrificial animals, and I would have left the consecrated state along with the people when they did.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 7230, book 94, باب قَوْلِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لَوِ اسْتَقْبَلْتُ مِنْ أَمْرِي مَا اسْتَدْبَرْتُ ‏"‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عُمَرَ، حَدَّثَنَا يَزِيدُ، عَنْ حَبِيبٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ كُنَّا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلَبَّيْنَا بِالْحَجِّ وَقَدِمْنَا مَكَّةَ لأَرْبَعٍ خَلَوْنَ مِنْ ذِي الْحِجَّةِ، فَأَمَرَنَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ نَطُوفَ بِالْبَيْتِ وَبِالصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، وَأَنْ نَجْعَلَهَا عُمْرَةً وَلْنَحِلَّ، إِلاَّ مَنْ كَانَ مَعَهُ هَدْىٌ قَالَ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ مَعَ أَحَدٍ مِنَّا هَدْىٌ غَيْرَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَطَلْحَةَ، وَجَاءَ عَلِيٌّ مِنَ الْيَمَنِ مَعَهُ الْهَدْىُ فَقَالَ أَهْلَلْتُ بِمَا أَهَلَّ بِهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالُوا نَنْطَلِقُ إِلَى مِنًى وَذَكَرُ أَحَدِنَا يَقْطُرُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنِّي لَوِ اسْتَقْبَلْتُ مِنْ أَمْرِي مَا اسْتَدْبَرْتُ مَا أَهْدَيْتُ، وَلَوْلاَ أَنَّ مَعِي الْهَدْىَ لَحَلَلْتُ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ وَلَقِيَهُ سُرَاقَةُ وَهْوَ يَرْمِي جَمْرَةَ الْعَقَبَةِ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَلَنَا هَذِهِ خَاصَّةً قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ بَلْ لأَبَدٍ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ وَكَانَتْ عَائِشَةُ قَدِمَتْ مَكَّةَ وَهْىَ حَائِضٌ، فَأَمَرَهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ تَنْسُكَ الْمَنَاسِكَ كُلَّهَا، غَيْرَ أَنَّهَا لاَ تَطُوفُ وَلاَ تُصَلِّي حَتَّى تَطْهُرَ، فَلَمَّا نَزَلُوا الْبَطْحَاءَ قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَتَنْطَلِقُونَ بِحَجَّةٍ وَعُمْرَةٍ وَأَنْطَلِقُ بِحَجَّةٍ‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ أَمَرَ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقِ أَنْ يَنْطَلِقَ مَعَهَا إِلَى التَّنْعِيمِ، فَاعْتَمَرَتْ عُمْرَةً فِي ذِي الْحَجَّةِ بَعْدَ أَيَّامِ الْحَجِّ‏.‏
en_text: Al-Hasan ibn Umar narrated to us; Yazid narrated to us, from Habib, from Ata, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah proclaiming the pilgrimage, and we arrived in Mecca on the fourth day of Dhu al-Hijjah. The Prophet ordered us to circumambulate the House and Safa and Marwah, make it an umrah, and leave the consecrated state, except those who had brought sacrificial animals. None of us had brought an animal except the Prophet and Talhah. Ali came from Yemen with sacrificial animals and said, “I entered consecration for what the Messenger of Allah entered consecration for.” They said, “Shall we go to Mina while one of us is still dripping?” The Messenger of Allah said: “If I had known beforehand what I later came to know, I would not have brought a sacrificial animal; and were it not that I have one with me, I would leave the consecrated state.” Suraqah met him while he was stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah and asked, “Messenger of Allah, is this concession only for us?” He said: “No, it is for all time.” Aishah had arrived in Mecca menstruating. The Prophet ordered her to perform all the rites except circumambulation and prayer until she became pure. When they stopped at al-Batha, Aishah said, “Messenger of Allah, you are going with a pilgrimage and an umrah, while I am going with only a pilgrimage.” He then ordered Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr to go with her to al-Tanim, and she performed an umrah in Dhu al-Hijjah after the days of pilgrimage.
